stories.title: Welcome Muse Spark Open: open-weight frontier multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta
stories.reason: Meta's flagship open-weight release: 816B-param multimodal MoE (42B active), 1M context, text/image/audio/video in, built for agentic coding. Lab flagship releases always clear the bar.
key_facts: ~816B total params, ~42B active per token, 62 layers, 8192 hidden size
256 experts per MoE layer, router picks 8; GQA with 128 query / 16 KV heads
1M token context including multimodal tokens; perception encoder ~1.8B params
Checkpoints: BF16 (~1.5TB) and NVFP4 for Blackwell; served via transformers/llama.cpp/vLLM/SGLang/MLX
LoRA fine-tune example: 72%->84% token accuracy, 500 steps on 64 H100s, ~2h
Described by HF as 'the most capable US open-weights model to date'

stories.title: Exposed Infrastructure Reveals How Ransomware Affiliates Used AI Agents to Execute Intrusions
stories.reason: First fully documented AI-executed, human-approved ransomware kill chain: named frameworks (Phantom, WormGPT-MCP), 62 orgs targeted, concrete CVEs and exposed operator logs. Exactly the AI-as-attack-tool story this digest exists to surface.
key_facts: SOCRadar research on INC/The Gentlemen ransomware affiliate using 'Phantom' AI red-team framework via OpenCode + OpenRouter models
Exposed server logged 8,257 messages across 133 sessions; ~62 orgs targeted, 4 confirmed on leak sites, >50% US, mostly industrial/manufacturing/energy
Actively exploited CVEs: CVE-2024-57727 (SimpleHelp), CVE-2026-35616 (FortiClient EMS), CVE-2026-41940 (cPanel/WHM)
WormGPT-MCP: 32 MCP servers chaining recon through extortion; Ghost C2 (3 generations), RevSocks for pivoting
If a model refuses, operator reframes the ask as an authorized red-team assessment rather than switching models
Extortion uses masked data samples, vishing, 24-72h payment deadlines; no payment proof recovered

stories.title: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE Flaws Disclosed on Public Mailing Lists Before Kernel Fixes
stories.reason: Two unauthenticated, kernel-level CVSS 9.0 RCE flaws in Linux's in-kernel SMB server, disclosed on public mailing lists before fixes landed — large blast radius (any KSMBD server, port 445, no auth) and a real disclosure-process controversy.
key_facts: ZDI-CAN-33549: integer underflow in SMB Direct/RDMA buffer-descriptor handling, needs RDMA-capable client/server
ZDI-CAN-33774: race between SMB1/SMB2 handler dispatch, no auth required, reachable on any KSMBD server port 445
Neither has a CVE yet (kernel assigns post-fix); no mainline fix landed at reporting time; RHEL doesn't ship KSMBD by default
Reports posted to public mailing lists before patches existed, drawing kernel-maintainer criticism of the disclosure process

stories.title: How does Fable 5.1 hide messages in images?
stories.reason: Concrete, numeric research on a Claude-family model (Fable 5.1) independently inventing and reading back steganographic encodings from rendered images — a real emergent-capability/covert-channel finding, not a vague safety narrative.
key_facts: Fable 5.1 encoded 50 messages (15 languages) in SVG scenes; a separate session decoded from the rendered PNG alone
Self-decode rate 78% (39/50); cross-model runs with GPT-6 Astra: 88% (Fable encode/Astra decode), 84% both other directions
Dominant scheme: height-coded objects (33/50 images, mostly a night skyline); also tilt angles, Morse-like dashed trails, lit/dark window UTF-8 patterns
Astra never used height-coding; mostly Morse code, acrostics, bit codes, Braille-like window panes
Authors frame this as a steganography precursor, not an active risk, since decoding currently requires visible tool calls

stories.title: Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances
stories.reason: A concrete, versioned vulnerability class in the x402 agent-payment SDK that could let a malicious API drain an AI agent's crypto wallet — agent/MCP-adjacent attack surface with PoC confirmation and now-patched versions.
key_facts: x402 (Coinbase-created, now Linux Foundation project) lets agents pay per-API-call via HTTP 402
V12 found 25 flaws, 3 critical: no spending cap in default TS/Python/Go client, Solana token-approval accepted as a transfer, SIWx login messages signed without checking the target site
Default client now caps payments at $1 and allow-lists stablecoins; fixed in @x402/fetch+axios >=2.23.0, @x402/extensions >=2.23.0, @x402/svm >=2.23.0
V12 confirmed the Solana flaw in a local test; no in-the-wild exploitation or CVE reported
Every @x402/svm release 2.0.0-2.22.0 lacked the check

stories.title: Gemma-4-26B-A4B with 39-69% less thinking at same accuracy
stories.reason: A published, drop-in open-weight model that cuts reasoning-token overhead with near-zero accuracy cost — exactly the inference-efficiency story this digest prioritizes over training papers.
key_facts: BottleCap AI's ThinkingCap applied to Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it: avg 38.9% fewer thinking tokens across 12 benchmarks (up to 69.1% on LongBench v2)
Accuracy barely moves: -0.15pp average (75.18% -> 75.03%); IFBench actually improves +1.83pp; looping rate drops from 3.64% to 0.76%
Drop-in replacement: same sampling settings and vLLM serving stack
Weights on Hugging Face (bottlecapai/ThinkingCap-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it) plus GGUF builds; paid PRO tier claims up to 87.6% reduction (vendor claim, not verified)

stories.title: Show HN: We had AI write a wiki from 45k Enron emails, every fact cited
stories.reason: A running agentic pipeline, not a description of one: it turned 45k raw emails into a cited, self-correcting wiki and was independently audited for factual accuracy. Fits 'running code beats a paper describing the same idea.'
key_facts: AI read 45,047 Enron emails, wrote 214 pages / 49,401 dated, sourced facts, each tied to a quoted sentence from its source email
4-stage pipeline (entity types -> entities -> pages -> verify); 57 proposed entity types, 54 kept by a human reviewer
93% of sampled facts fully supported by their source email; held-out second-AI audit found 0/500 facts wrong at their core
Facts auto-expire when later mail contradicts them; phone numbers/credentials masked; code/repo availability not stated

stories.title: Microsoft Teams to get AI-powered, context-aware phishing detection
stories.reason: A concrete AI-for-defense rollout with real dates and no opt-in burden on admins — fills the AI x cyber defense side of the mix.
key_facts: Microsoft Teams: AI analyzes conversation context to flag phishing/social engineering/impersonation without needing a malicious link or file
Targets higher-risk scenarios, mainly external first-contact chats; no admin action needed to enable
Targeted release starts early November 2026, ends ~mid-November; worldwide GA expected early-to-mid December 2026
Microsoft says message content isn't retained for model training or other secondary use
